name: Water
description: A small, bent molecule whose polarity helps it dissolve many ionic and polar substances.

name: Methane
description: The simplest hydrocarbon, with a tetrahedral arrangement around carbon.

name: Carbon dioxide
description: A linear molecule whose polar bonds cancel to make the whole molecule nonpolar.

name: Ethanol
description: A two-carbon alcohol with a polar hydroxyl group.

name: Glucose
description: A carbohydrate used by cells as a major source of chemical energy.

name: Caffeine
description: A nitrogen-containing organic molecule found in coffee and tea.

name: Oxygen
description: A diatomic gas used in respiration; the displayed O=O structure is a simple Lewis-style representation.

name: Ammonia
description: A trigonal-pyramidal nitrogen compound used to make fertilizers and cleaning products.

name: Hydrogen peroxide
description: An oxygen-containing compound commonly sold as a dilute disinfectant.

name: Methanol
description: The simplest alcohol; toxic despite its resemblance to ethanol.

name: Ethane
description: A two-carbon alkane found in natural gas.

name: Propene
description: A three-carbon alkene used to make polypropylene and other chemicals.

name: Acetone
description: A small ketone commonly used as a solvent.

name: 2-Propanol
description: A secondary alcohol also known as isopropyl alcohol.

name: Ethyl ethanoate
description: An ester formed from ethanoic acid and ethanol.

name: Ethanoic acid
description: The acid that gives vinegar its sour taste.

name: Dimethyl ether
description: An ether isomer of ethanol: the same formula, but different atom connections.

name: Bromomethane
description: A methyl halide that provides a simple SN2 teaching example.

name: Sodium chloride
description: An ionic solid made of sodium and chloride ions, not a discrete covalent molecule.

name: Sodium hydroxide
description: An ionic compound that supplies hydroxide ions in solution; it is highly caustic.
